format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(effectsize)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)

fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
fmt_p <- function(p) if (p < .001) "< .001" else paste("=", sub("^0", "", fmt_num(p, 3)))
fmt_bounded <- function(x, digits = 2) sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", fmt_num(x, digits))

crew <- read_csv("astronauts.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: people
people <- crew |>
  filter(mission_number == 1) |>
  transmute(number, sex, military_civilian,
            age = year_of_mission - year_of_birth,
            total_missions = total_number_of_missions)
n_women <- sum(people$sex == "female")
```

## Method

### Participants

The Crew Log (Stavnichuk & Corlett, 2020) records `r nrow(people)` astronauts who flew from 1961 to 2019, `r n_women` of them women (`r fmt_num(100 * n_women / nrow(people), 1)`%). Each astronaut is one case, described at their first flight; ages are approximate (year of flight minus year of birth).

## Results

```{r}
#| label: tbl-age
age_by_sex <- people |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  summarise(n = n(), M = mean(age), SD = sd(age))
knitr::kable(age_by_sex, digits = 2, col.names = c("Sex", "*n*", "*M*", "*SD*"),
             caption = "Age at First Flight by Sex")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-age
age_plot <- ggplot(people, aes(x = sex, y = age)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "Sex", y = "Age at first flight (years)") +
  theme_classic()
age_plot
```

```{r}
#| label: tests
age_test <- t.test(age ~ sex, data = people)
age_d <- cohens_d(age ~ sex, data = people)$Cohens_d
missions_cor <- cor.test(people$age, people$total_missions, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
```

**Age at first flight.** Women and men were compared with Welch's *t*-test: *t*(`r fmt_num(age_test$parameter)`) = `r fmt_num(age_test$statistic)`, *p* `r fmt_p(age_test$p.value)`, *d* = `r fmt_num(age_d)`.

**Age and career length.** Because the number of missions is a skewed count, its relationship with age at first flight was tested with Spearman's rank correlation, *r*~s~ = `r fmt_bounded(missions_cor$estimate)`, *p* `r fmt_p(missions_cor$p.value)`.
